title: Marinated Steak Tips
equipment: Gallon zip-top bag or large bowl

items: 2 lb sirloin steak tips (flap meat), cut into 1½-inch chunks
1 tsp neutral oil, for the griddle
½ tsp kosher salt, for finishing

steps: Whisk the soy sauce, Worcestershire, olive oil, brown sugar, Dijon, vinegar, garlic, pepper and onion powder in a bowl or zip-top bag. Don't add salt yet; the soy carries plenty.
Add the steak tips, press out the air and refrigerate 4–8 hr. Don't go past 12 hr, or the outside turns mushy.
Take the meat out 30–40 min before cooking. Discard the marinade, set the pieces on a rack or paper towels and pat them dry. Wet meat steams instead of searing.
Heat a griddle or cast-iron skillet over high heat 10 min, with a cooler zone if you can. It's ready when a drop of water skitters and vanishes. Wipe on a thin film of oil.

Lay the pieces down with space between them and don't touch them for 2–3 min. Turn to sear the other sides, about 2 min more, moving pieces to the cooler zone as they finish. Pull them at 125°F for medium-rare.
Tent loosely with foil and rest 5–8 min; the temperature climbs about 5°F. Season with the kosher salt and slice against the grain if the pieces are large.
tips: Doneness, pull temp then final temp after resting: rare 115°F to 120°F, medium-rare 125°F to 130°F, medium 135°F to 140°F, medium-well 145°F to 150°F.
Ask for flap meat or sirloin tips, not stew beef. Flap meat is tender enough to sear but turns to leather if overcooked.
No griddle? Broil on the top rack on high 3–4 min per side, or use cast iron in batches so the pan stays hot.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Leftovers are best sliced cold for sandwiches, since reheating pushes them past medium. If you reheat, do it briefly in a hot skillet.
